# Pre-Implementation Requirements-Quality Gate: Hero Change Deployment

**Purpose**: Formal requirements-quality gate between `/speckit.plan` and `/speckit.tasks`. Evaluates whether the written specification and planning artifacts are complete, clear, internally consistent, measurable, traceable, and sufficiently bounded for task decomposition and implementation.
**Created**: 2026-08-18
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)
**Depth**: HIGH / FORMAL GATE
**Audience**: Senior technical reviewer / hackathon architecture reviewer

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Scope note**: These items test the *requirements as written* — not code, not behavior, not implementation correctness. No item below is a test case, and none should be read as one.

**Authoritative context reviewed**: `.specify/memory/constitution.md`, `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `research.md`, `data-model.md`, `contracts/agents.md`, `quickstart.md`.

## Spec ↔ Plan Boundary & Traceability

- [x] CHK001 Is there a per-requirement traceability mapping from each of FR-001–FR-011 and SC-001–SC-015 to the plan components, milestones, and test groups that address them — rather than coarse range references such as "FR-001–FR-011"? [Traceability, Gap, Plan §Test Strategy vs Spec §Requirements]
- [x] CHK002 Are plan-introduced elements traceable to spec authority — the non-functional targets (<5 min workflow, <10 s field verification), the web/CLI demo surfaces, and the technical representation of all 13 canonical states — or does the plan add acceptance-shaped content the spec never authorized, with a Constitution Check that predates the current artifacts? [Consistency, Conflict, Plan §Technical Context / §Project Structure / §Constitution Check vs Spec §Success Criteria / §Non-Goals]

## Non-Goals vs Track Enhancements (REQUIRED GATE CONCERN)

- [x] CHK003 Do the artifacts distinguish explicitly, in one authoritative place, between (A) "NOT REQUIRED for S1 product acceptance / FR / SC completion" and (B) "OPTIONAL hackathon architectural enhancement if access and time permit" — or does the wording remain contradictory, with the same GEAP components listed as Non-Goals in the spec and as `TRACK_ENHANCEMENT` in the plan? [Ambiguity, Conflict, Spec §Non-Goals vs Plan §Google Service Decision Matrix / §GEAP Availability Gate]
- [x] CHK004 Is that distinction written strongly enough that task generation cannot emit GEAP work as mandatory or sequence it ahead of deterministic core work, that failure of every access gate provably leaves FR/SC acceptance unchanged, and that a judge cannot mistake a fallback for a delivered platform capability? [Clarity, Consistency, Gap, Plan §GEAP Availability Gate / §Implementation Milestones, Quickstart §OPTIONAL track]

## Deterministic Truth Boundary & Agent Responsibility

- [x] CHK005 Is authoritative ownership assigned exclusively, without overlap or silence, for all twelve truth concerns — state transitions, source-version applicability, authorization, the 9 remediation preconditions, idempotency, retry deduplication, supersession, event chronology, expected-vs-observed comparison, the 7 proof invariants, evidence integrity, and Change Proof generation? [Completeness, Contracts §5 Truth Engine, Plan §Deterministic Truth Engine]
- [x] CHK006 Is any requirement phrased such that an LLM or agent could be read as *owning* one of those truths (e.g. "the agent applies the patch", "the agent identifies the affected artifact") rather than proposing an output the Truth Engine adjudicates? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-002 / §FR-003, Contracts §1–2]
- [x] CHK007 Does each of the four agents have exactly one irreducible semantic responsibility with explicit tool boundaries, read/write permissions, output contract, and defined failure behavior — with no duplicated authority, Change Proof generation stated as deterministic and unreachable by any agent, and the Truth Engine consistently presented as a non-agent service? [Completeness, Consistency, Contracts §Agent Topology / §5, Spec §Change Proof]

## State Model & Completion Conditions

- [x] CHK008 Is every one of the 13 states classified as recoverable / blocking / terminal in a single authoritative place, with terminal states stated to have no legal exits and `SUPERSEDED` / `FAILED` stated as permanently unable to reach `PROOF_COMPLETE`? [Completeness, Consistency, Spec §State Requirements / §Change Proof cond. 7, Data-Model §Validation Rules]
- [x] CHK009 Is the "REVIEW_REQUIRED has no autonomous exit in S1" rule reconciled with "SUPERSEDED may be entered from any non-terminal state" — i.e. is the legal exit set for `REVIEW_REQUIRED` defined rather than left to inference? [Conflict, Data-Model §State Transitions, Spec §State Requirements]
- [x] CHK010 Does `data-model.md` reflect the corrected condition-7 semantics (current-state evaluation; historical `VERIFICATION_FAILED` / `VERIFICATION_INCONCLUSIVE` permitted when a later authoritative PASS exists), or must the reader infer that from `spec.md` alone? [Consistency, Gap, Spec §Change Proof cond. 7 vs Data-Model §Validation Rules]
- [x] CHK011 Are the criteria for "the latest authoritative field verification" defined objectively — which ordering signal governs (server-assigned `event_sequence` vs client `timestamp`) — so that a late-arriving older verification provably cannot override a newer one? [Clarity, Measurability, Spec §Edge Cases, Data-Model §VerificationEvent]
- [x] CHK012 Are the seven `PROOF_COMPLETE` conditions stated as the single authoritative completion gate, with no artifact introducing an additional, weaker, or parallel completion path? [Consistency, Spec §Change Proof, Plan §Change Proof Technical Design]

## Async, Restart & Idempotency

- [x] CHK013 Do the requirements state that Firestore — not ADK session or resumability state — is authoritative, that the orchestrator must not be interpreted as an indefinitely blocked in-process wait, and that evidence arrival triggers a distinct invocation rather than resuming a live process? [Clarity, Gap, Plan §Orchestration Strategy, Contracts §Async boundary, Constitution §VI]
- [x] CHK014 Is idempotency scope defined beyond change events — duplicate field-evidence submissions, duplicate delivery attempts, repeated proof generation — and are restart-recovery requirements defined for a process that dies mid-step with a partially applied side effect? [Coverage, Gap, Edge Case, Spec §FR-007 / §FR-008 / §US9]

## Proof, Evidence & Integrity Claims

- [x] CHK015 Do the artifacts state what SHA-256 hashing does **not** guarantee (no digital signature, no third-party attestation, no notarization, no immutable ledger or blockchain) and define "immutable" operationally (write-once document, generation-matched object) — so no accidental cryptographic-attestation claim can reach judges? [Gap, Risk, Ambiguity, Spec §Change Proof, Plan §Change Proof Technical Design]
- [x] CHK016 For a `NO_OP` remediation, are the required proof and evidence fields specified — noting that the `ChangeProof` model declares `before_ref` / `after_ref` as non-optional while no mutation occurred? [Conflict, Gap, Data-Model §ChangeProof vs Spec §US3 scenario 2]
- [x] CHK017 Does the evidence-manifest requirement explicitly include failed and inconclusive verification attempts and rejected tool responses — not only the passing event — are the proof validator's responsibilities specified distinctly from proof generation, and is the relationship between runtime telemetry and business evidence defined (required proof input vs supporting observability)? [Coverage, Completeness, Clarity, Spec §Change Proof cond. 6–7, Data-Model §EvidenceManifest, Plan §Change Proof Technical Design / §Observability]

## Data Classification & Event Source Honesty

- [x] CHK018 Are the criteria for applying each label (`REAL`, `SYNTHETIC`, `DERIVED`, `SIMULATED`) and for combining them non-exclusively defined precisely enough to be applied consistently — including when `SIMULATED` is mandatory rather than optional? [Clarity, Measurability, Spec §Data Classification, Constitution §XIII]
- [x] CHK019 Do the artifacts state explicitly that the business content is `SYNTHETIC` while Pub/Sub delivery, model calls, and cloud writes are `REAL`, that the workflow begins from an external event rather than a chatbot prompt, and that no ERP/WMS/HR/Workspace integration is claimed? [Clarity, Completeness, Research §R-012, Spec §Non-Goals / §Hackathon Alignment]

## Autonomous Remediation Safety

- [x] CHK020 Are all 9 autonomy preconditions individually evaluable against a named data source — in particular, are "corresponding target instruction is uniquely identifiable" (#7) and "does not contain conflicting/additional divergence" (#8) defined measurably rather than left to judgment? [Ambiguity, Measurability, Spec §Autonomy Boundaries]
- [x] CHK021 Is the already-compliant no-op path defined consistently across spec, data-model, and contracts (what is recorded, which state follows, how the workflow continues), and are requirements defined for impact outcomes other than exactly one affected artifact — zero, or more than one — or is "exactly one" an undocumented assumption inherited from the reference scenario? [Consistency, Gap, Assumption, Spec §US2 / §US3 / §FR-002, Contracts §2, Data-Model §Workflow]

## Tool Poisoning & Untrusted Input

- [x] CHK022 Do the artifacts require the full validation chain (schema, provenance, expected source, expected artifact/tool identity, authorization scope, source-version applicability, deterministic semantic invariants) for **every** tool response, or is it attached only to `RemediationResult` while `DeliveryResult` and `FieldObservation` reference schema validation alone? [Coverage, Consistency, Plan §Tool Response Validation Chain vs Contracts §2–4]
- [x] CHK023 Is it stated that the validation chain is mandatory in the fallback architecture (no Agent Gateway, no Model Armor), so that an optional platform control can never be read as a precondition for this defense? [Clarity, Plan §Tool Response Validation Chain, Research §R-014]

## Agent Identity, Gateway, Model Armor & Access Gates

- [x] CHK024 Is GEAP Agent Identity distinguished from Cloud Run service accounts in every artifact — service accounts labelled only as runtime or fallback identities, no document calling a service account "Agent Identity", per-agent identity presented as an optional track enhancement, and the fallback's weaker security properties documented rather than glossed? [Consistency, Clarity, Plan §Agent Identity and Runtime Identity Model, Contracts §Identity Model, Research §R-013]
- [x] CHK025 Is the organization-parent requirement of the Agent Identity principal recorded as an unverified account-level dependency with a defined access check and fallback, rather than assumed available? [Dependency, Assumption, Plan §GEAP Availability Gate, Quickstart §MS-23]
- [x] CHK026 For the single governed path, are caller identity, target tool, required identity, allow policy, deny case, and expected audit evidence each specified for both ALLOW (Remediation Agent) and DENY (Frontline Enablement Agent) — with the fallback denial honestly labelled application-level rather than platform-enforced? [Completeness, Clarity, Plan §Agent Gateway Governed Path, Contracts §Planned Tool Contract]
- [x] CHK027 Is the unresolved MCP-vs-plain-HTTP protocol decision for the Artifact Mutation Tool bounded sufficiently for task generation, given that per-tool authorization granularity depends on which is chosen? [Dependency, Decision Required, Plan §Agent Gateway Governed Path]
- [x] CHK028 Do the artifacts constrain Model Armor to untrusted-text screening and explicitly deny it authority over domain authorization, state transitions, proof completion, and semantic correctness of structured business data — and is its documented fail-open outage behavior addressed so no evidence can claim screening that did not occur? [Clarity, Completeness, Plan §Model Armor Enforcement Path, Research §R-003]
- [x] CHK029 Does every gated component (Agent Runtime, Agent Registry, Agent Identity, Agent Gateway, Model Armor, advanced Agent Observability) carry an ACCESS_CHECK, SUCCESS CONDITION, FALLBACK, and an explicit non-blocking status at the component level — not only as a global preamble? [Completeness, Plan §GEAP Availability Gate]

## Model Requirements (Gemini / Gemma / Veo)

- [x] CHK030 Are the core model selection rationale, structured-output contract, error/unavailability behavior, retry and timeout policy, and the exact boundary where model output stops being trusted specified consistently — noting that retry limits currently appear only inside the cost table? [Clarity, Consistency, Gap, Research §R-001, Plan §Orchestration Strategy / §Cost Strategy]
- [x] CHK031 Do the requirements establish the raw image → normalized observation → deterministic comparator chain with bounded observation values and explicit `INCONCLUSIVE` semantics, a measurable promotion gate before relying on Gemma in the live demo, an honest manual/deterministic fallback, the GPU/quota dependency, and unresolved serving/variant/quantization choices recorded as open assumptions rather than settled facts? [Measurability, Gap, Dependency, Assumption, Research §R-008, Contracts §4, Plan §Risk Register]
- [x] CHK032 Is Veo specified as strictly optional and non-blocking — text delta alone satisfying FR-004, pre-generated or cached output labelled honestly, generated-asset data classification defined, live-generation latency not assumed, and Veo failure explicitly unable to prevent `PROOF_COMPLETE`? [Completeness, Gap, Research §R-009, Spec §FR-004 / §FR-010]

## Frontline UX & Accessibility

- [x] CHK033 Are the minimum frontline interactions specified — receiving the delta, understanding the expected change, submitting field evidence, and receiving PASS / FAIL / INCONCLUSIVE feedback — noting that worker-facing feedback after a FAIL is currently implied by US6 rather than required anywhere? [Gap, Coverage, Spec §US4–US6, Constitution §X]
- [x] CHK034 Are accessibility and minimum mobile usability requirements intentionally deferred **in writing**, or merely absent — given that the Constitution's quality gate names accessibility/frontline UX as a review dimension? [Gap, Ambiguity, Spec §Non-Goals, Constitution §Development Workflow]

## Manual Setup, Cost, Reproducibility & Implementation Priority

- [x] CHK035 Do the quickstart steps consistently carry WHY / WHEN / EXPECTED RESULT / HOW TO VERIFY / COST RISK, cleanly separate CORE from OPTIONAL / TRACK ENHANCEMENT, avoid any optional step appearing as a core prerequisite in ordering or wording, and cover every required setup area — project/billing, credits, APIs, auth/ADC, secrets, IAM, Firestore, Pub/Sub, Storage, Cloud Run instance limits, GPU quota, Gemma, Veo, observability, each GEAP component, and cleanup? [Consistency, Completeness, Coverage, Quickstart §Manual Setup Required]
- [x] CHK036 Are cost caps, `max-instances` limits, the budget alert, generation caps, and the cleanup/shutdown procedure expressed as binding requirements with owners and timing rather than advisory prose — and is the `ESTIMATED` vs `ACTUAL COST OBSERVED` distinction unambiguous, including which unit rates remain uncaptured at plan time? [Measurability, Clarity, Dependency, Plan §Cost Strategy, Quickstart §MS-4 / §MS-13 / §MS-15 / §MS-20, Research §R-015]
- [x] CHK037 Are the reproducibility artifacts specified by required content rather than filename alone — reference fixtures with expected outcomes (SC-014), `JUDGES_START_HERE.md`, `LIMITATIONS.md`, `MANIFEST.json`, `geap_access_gate.json`, `cost_model.json` — sufficiently for a judge to distinguish a claim from its proof? [Completeness, Measurability, Gap, Spec §SC-014, Quickstart §Evidence Pack Structure]
- [x] CHK038 Does the plan define milestone exit criteria and an explicit ordering rule that prevents frontend, GEAP, Veo, or visual-polish work from being sequenced ahead of the M0 deterministic Truth Engine during task generation? [Gap, Risk, Plan §Implementation Milestones]
- [x] CHK039 Do the written failure requirements cover every enumerated failure mode — malformed LLM output, timeout, model unavailable, duplicate event, remediation failure, delivery failure, evidence unavailable, inconclusive verification, incorrect verification, source supersession, corrupted evidence, GEAP unavailable, Gemma unavailable, Veo unavailable — and is it stated that optional-enhancement failure never silently becomes core failure? [Coverage, Completeness, Spec §FR-011 / §Edge Cases, Plan §Risk Register / §GEAP Availability Gate]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`; this file is a separate reviewer-owned artifact and must not be merged into it
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference; record findings inline beneath the item they concern
- Marker legend: `[Gap]` requirement appears missing · `[Ambiguity]` wording admits multiple readings · `[Conflict]` two artifacts disagree · `[Assumption]` unvalidated premise · `[Dependency]` external or account-level precondition · `[Decision Required]` open choice that bounds task generation
- Highest-risk entries: CHK003, CHK015, CHK016, CHK022, CHK025, CHK027, CHK038 — each can silently corrupt task generation, judged claims, or the deterministic core if left unresolved
